course_name_original: Algebră liniară, geometrie analitică și diferentială
course_name_en: Linear Algebra, Analytical and Differential Geometry

learning_outcomes.text: Defines basic concepts from the studied algebra and geometry chapters.
Understands the mathematical objects described in the course.
Acquires theoretical concepts and develops skills to work with them.
Develops logical mental attitudes for problem-solving.
Explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results in mathematics.
Applies calculation formulas, theorems, and criteria studied in the algebra and geometry chapters to complex problems.
Operates with basic concepts, principles, and methods from the studied algebra and geometry chapters.
Solves mathematics problems with applicability in engineering and validates the obtained solution.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their own field of activity by adequately using efficient learning methods and techniques throughout life.

syllabus_topics: Matrices. Determinants. Systems of linear algebraic equations.
Study of compatibility/incompatibility of second- and third-order linear algebraic systems. Methods for solving second- and third-order systems.

Matrices and determinants. Operations with matrices. Calculation of determinants of order n, n < 4. Rank of a matrix. Rank of the product of two matrices. Adjoint matrix. Inverse matrix. Block matrix. Calculation with block matrices.
Elementary transformations. Gauss elimination method. Application to calculating the rank of a matrix, calculating the inverse of a matrix, calculating determinants, solving linear algebraic systems.
Linear spaces.
Linear subspaces. Operations with linear subspaces. Fundamental subspaces of a matrix (column subspace, null subspace).
Bases in a linear space. Dimension of a linear space. Coordinates of a vector in a given basis. Change of basis.
Euclidean linear spaces.
Scalar product. Norms. Vector norm, matrix norm. Examples of Euclidean spaces.
Cauchy-Schwarz-Buniakowski inequality. Orthonormal bases. Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process.
Linear transformations.
Definitions, examples (rotations, projections, symmetries). Matrix of a linear transformation with respect to two bases. Operations with linear transformations.
Kernel and image of a linear transformation. Rank and defect of a linear transformation.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix.
Characteristic polynomial of a matrix. Cayley Hamilton theorem. Application to calculating the inverse of a matrix. Algorithm for diagonalizing a matrix.
Polynomials of matrices. Exponential matrix for diagonalizable matrices.
Real quadratic forms.
Matrix expression of a quadratic form. Classification of quadratic forms.
Bringing a quadratic form to canonical form. Inertia theorem.
Analytical geometry.
Coordinate system in the plane. Cartesian coordinates. Line in the plane.
Coordinate system in space. Vectors in plane and space. Scalar product. Applications of the scalar product.
Vector product. Line and plane in space.
Complex numbers. Algebraic form. Operations with complex numbers. Representation in the plane of complex numbers, geometric interpretation.
Conics and quadrics.
Conics by reduced equations: circles, ellipses, hyperbolas, parabolas. Conics by general equations.
Quadrics in space. Second-degree surfaces (quadrics) by reduced equations: sphere, ellipsoids, hyperboloids, paraboloids, cones, cylinders.
Elements of differential geometry
teaching_methods: Exposition with electronic board associated with an integrated e-learning system
Interactive seminar where exercises are discussed and worked by professor and students at the board

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments, preparation of a paper - case study)
Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)

Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its study credits.
